newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly up on Tuesday on improved market sentiment, but trading was slow, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 24,050 yuan ($2,901) per tonne, rising 40 yuan.
It opened at 24,030 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 24,070 and a low of 23,980 yuan per tonne.
June rose 30 to 23,400, July 40 to 23,650, August 10 to 23,840, October 40 to 24,050 and November 50 to 24,010.
Combined volume fell to 19,280 tonnes from 34,540 tonnes.
Copper opened little changed and rose slightly but steadily for most of the session, traders said.
Market sentiment improved after the key September contract closed above the 24,000-yuan resistance level on Monday, the trading sources said.
Many investors built positions in the belief that copper will rise in the next few days, they said.

"Despite a halt in trading on the LME (London Metal Exchange) on Monday, copper rose slightly due to improved market sentiment," one trader said. "But slow trading indicated some wary investors were still staying on the sidelines," he added.
The LME was closed on Monday for a bank holiday. Traders in London said they expected copper to consolidate above $2,500, perhaps testing $2,550 despite its overbought position, on Tuesday.
Physical copper prices in the Shanghai area strengthened to around 23,350 yuan after starting the day between 23,100 and 23,200 yuan per tonne.
Traders said with late-maturing contracts ending above the 24,000-yuan level on Tuesday, they were optimisitc about the short-term market trend.
"Technical charts indicate copper is likely to test the 24,300-yuan level, which is the highest price level since March," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected copper to rise steadily in the next few days.
Aluminium ended little changed. June closed unchanged at 15,400, July did not trade and September fell 90 to 15,690.
Combined volume rose to 740 tonnes from 150 tonnes.
